transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yes… I suppose occupational health thought it would be a good idea for me to come in. It’s probably not as serious as it sounds, but I’ve gotten into a bit of a pattern where I push breakfast and lunch aside when I’m busy with lab runs or exhibition work, and then by the time I do eat, I tend to keep it very small and controlled. 

I’m not sure if that’s the sort of thing you mean.
After you eat, do you ever make yourself vomit, take laxatives, or exercise excessively to prevent weight gain?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t make myself sick or anything like that. And laxatives—no. Exercise… I wouldn’t say excessively, really. I try to keep active, but not specifically to undo eating, if that makes sense. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking?
Do you ever feel a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if others might not see you as overweight?

I… yes, I suppose I do, though I try not to think of it as fear exactly. It’s more that if the scale goes up even a tiny amount, even just a fraction, I get this sudden panic, like I’m losing control or losing the discipline I’ve worked quite hard to keep. 

I know that probably sounds a bit much. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
How long have you been feeling this way about your eating habits and weight, and has it affected your work or personal life?

It’s been… long enough that it feels like a habit now, I suppose. I’m still getting the important things done at work, the deadlines and lab responsibilities, so I wouldn’t want to overstate it.

But I have stopped going to lab lunches, and some of the more informal gallery planning meals too. I usually tell myself I’m just busy, which is partly true, but… I think it’s made me a bit more separate from colleagues than I used to be. Does that make sense?
Do you find that your eating habits are connected to a need to feel in control or disciplined in other areas of your life as well?

I suppose… yes, probably. I don’t like saying it quite that way, because it makes it sound very rigid, and I do function. But occupational health sent me because I’ve got into this pattern where, during lab runs or exhibition work, I sort of push breakfast and lunch aside. Then when I finally do eat, I keep it very small and… controlled.

It feels less messy that way, I suppose. Like I’m being disciplined rather than letting things get away from me. Is that the kind of connection you mean?
